subject: KV cache divergence in private deployment — CareFirst incident and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: ops@carefirst.co
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: KV cache divergence in private deployment — CareFirst incident and next steps

Maya / CareFirst ops team,

We observed a transient control-plane mismatch affecting your private VPC deployment during an automated rolling upgrade this morning. Summary:
- Window: ~09:05–09:25 PST (Nov 11 2026)
- Impact: brief agent handshakes failures and a small spike in 500/503 responses for inference requests routed to 3 private nodes; average latency increased by ~120ms for affected requests.
- Scope: only the private VPC cluster provisioned in us-west-2; no public Redwood-hosted tenants were impacted.
- Data security: we have no evidence of data exfiltration — the incident was a state/serialization inconsistency in the KV cache used by the runtime.

What happened (short): during the upgrade to runtime v1.12.0 we introduced a serialization tweak for the KV cache that in rare sequences produced incompatible cache keys across rolling-upgraded hosts. When a newer host served a request with an incompatible KV entry, the agent handshake failed and control-plane routed retries to fallback hosts. This produced short-lived request errors while retries completed.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Rolled back the runtime on the private cluster to v1.11.4 within the incident window.
- Invalidated KV caches across the 3 affected nodes to force re-sync.
- Applied a hotfix to the upgrade orchestrator to prevent parallel serialization schema changes during rolling upgrades.
- Collected logs and a KV dump for your review (attached).

Attachments: controlplane-kvcache-dump-20261111.tar.gz (log + cache dump)

Asks / next steps for CareFirst:
1) Can you confirm whether your side saw any client retries that exceeded your SLA thresholds or triggered alerts?
2) Would you like Redwood to run a rehydrate and full KV-sync during a low-traffic window (we can schedule tonight)?

We know this type of failure is disruptive — apologies for the incident. I’m available for a 30-minute bridge to walk through the logs and runbook; suggested link here: https://cal.com/redwood/kimberly/30min.

Best,
Kimberly Park

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: root cause and mitigation plan for KV cache divergence

Internal notes (do not share external verbatim):
Root cause: a non-backwards-compatible change in the cache key derivation introduced in runtime v1.12.0 when continuous-batching was enabled. The new code path introduced a different separator character in serialized keys under a narrow sequence/slot alignment. During rolling upgrades, mixed-version hosts could produce divergent key sets for identical logical cache entries. That divergence led to agent handshake mismatches that surfaced as transient control-plane errors.

Mitigations implemented:
- Immediate rollback of runtime to v1.11.4 (completed 09:20 PST).
- Cache invalidation + node restart for the three affected agents.
- Orchestrator hotfix to serialize schema changes (prevent cross-version mixtures during upgrades).

Proposed longer-term actions:
1) Add a compatibility test in our CI that runs a mixed-version KV cache validation harness.
2) Add an automated pre-upgrade dry-run that validates serialization compatibility per cluster.
3) Create a targeted alert for higher-than-normal agent RPC handshake errors (we saw a sharp spike that should have been visible earlier).

Attachments for internal review: postmortem-draft-20261111.md (link in related_links).

I suggest offering CareFirst a service credit and a scheduled maintenance window to run a full KV rehydrate if they want.

— Sean
Senior Reliability Engineer
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carefirst.co>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Incident update and proposed remediation — KV cache divergence (CareFirst private cluster)

Maya — thank you for the quick confirmation and for sharing your metrics. Summary and next steps below:

What we’ve completed:
- Confirmed rollback to v1.11.4 and cache invalidation across the three nodes by 09:25 PST; the cluster returned to normal health metrics shortly after.
- Collected and attached the KV dump and control-plane logs for your SREs.
- Applied an orchestrator hotfix to block parallel schema changes during rolling upgrades.

On your questions:
- Double-processing: our request tracing shows that no inference requests were double-processed. Retries were routed and completed by fallback hosts; token counts align with a single processing per user request.
- Downtime risk from manual KV invalidation: the invalidate+reconnect we ran produced a short reconnection window (~20–40 seconds per node) while the cache rebuilt. We can perform a controlled rehydrate in a low-traffic window; this should have similar, very short connectivity blips but not prolonged downtime.

Proposed customer-facing actions:
1) We recommend a scheduled maintenance tonight (02:00–03:00 PST) to run a full KV rehydrate and an extra validation pass (optional). If you approve, we’ll coordinate a short maintenance notification and run the job.
2) We will provide a one-time service credit equivalent to 5% of your monthly usage for November as a good-faith gesture.
3) We will share the post-incident report (draft attached) and invite your team to comment; a final version will be published within 72 hours.

Attachments: privatenet-reconnect-runbook.pdf (steps + expected impact), postmortem-draft-20261111.md, controlplane-kvcache-dump-20261111.tar.gz

If 4pm PST works, I’ll send a calendar invite; otherwise pick a time here: https://cal.com/redwood/kimberly/30min.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the final postmortem and the runbook edits to prevent recurrence.

Regards,
